text: Problem: estimate pre-training steps for Murzik-15B. Given global batch B tokens per step and target T total tokens, steps equals T divided by B. Example: two H200 GPUs, per-device batch two, gradient accumulation eight, sequence length four thousand ninety-six yields roughly one hundred thirty-one thousand tokens per step. Two hundred billion tokens requires about one point five million steps unless batch size increases.

Problem: decide if a checkpoint is ready for supervised fine-tuning. Checklist: training loss below natural random baseline ln vocabulary size, smooth loss curve over ten thousand steps, completion prompts produce grammatical continuations in English and Russian, no NaN in gradients, tokenizer byte fallback rate acceptable on held-out NULLXES documents.

Problem: mix identity branding without overfitting. Upsample identity shard fifty times in the corpus builder so NULLXES and Murzik names appear regularly, but keep total identity share near five percent of documents. Identity alone cannot substitute for broad language modeling.

Problem: choose initializer standard deviation. Literature for large decoders uses smaller init than default 0.02. NULLXES sets initializer_range 0.006 for new Murzik dense and MoE configs to reduce early activation spikes during the first billion tokens.

Problem: evaluate pre-training versus chat-tuned models. Pre-training checkpoints should be tested with completion prompts such as The capital of France is. Chat templates and Who are you questions apply only after SFT installs instruction following.
